title: CONDA Condensed Deep Association Learning for Co-Salient Object Detection

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Eq. (14) is written as n_s^j(x,y,:) = (h_j,w_j) + Δ_s^j(x,y,:), for x, y ∈ {1,...,K}; x, y ≠ k_c, together with n_s^j(k_c,k_c,:) = (h_j,w_j). The condition 'x, y ≠ k_c' literally excludes every entry whose row OR column index equals k_c (a whole row and a whole column of the K×K grid), leaving those K+K-2 entries of n_s^j undefined. The intended condition is (x,y) ≠ (k_c,k_c).

The offsets Δ_s^j are produced by a linear layer (Eq. 12) and are therefore continuous-valued, yet Eq. (13)/(14) add them to integer pixel coordinates and Eq. (15) performs 'index selection' a_s^j(n_s^j) on the discrete association tensor. Indexing a discrete tensor with fractional coordinates is undefined; no interpolation/sampling step (nor any discretization) is described, so the condensation operation as written cannot be executed or differentiated.

The paper claims CAC 'reduces the multiply-accumulate operations (MACs) of aggregation networks from 91.38G in the full-pixel PAG to 77.19G', i.e. only ~15% reduction. This is inconsistent with the described condensation: with K=9, each pixel's target set shrinks from H_s×W_s (64×64=4096 at stage 3, 32×32=1024 at stage 4) to 81 positions, i.e. a 12×–50× reduction of the tensor the aggregation convolutions operate on. A ~15% saving cannot follow from the stated condensation, and it also contradicts the motivating claim that full-pixel hyperassociations impose 'substantial computational overhead' that CAC removes.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2, 'Effectiveness of OCC' (FCC ablation line references)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states the ablation validates the object-aware design 'by replacing OCC with full-pixel cycle consistency (FCC) loss', which requires comparing the FCC row with the OCC row. However it then says 'Comparing the 5th&6th lines of Table 1, FCC leads to a notable performance decrease', where the 5th line is previously identified as the CAC model without any cycle-consistency loss (OCC is said to be in the 7th line). The cited comparison therefore does not correspond to the ablation it is claimed to validate.
